hqm.quest_set.basic_survival.desc: Guide to the initial stages of surviving on an unknown world.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.gathering_suppl:
Emergency Survival Checklist:

1. Perform self-diagnostics and administer emergency first aid to treat any injuries.
2. Assess the environment for potential threats, resources, and shelter. Exercise caution around the detached reactor, containment has breached and high-temperature fuel is leaking.
3. Ration available food and water. The water reclamation system is damaged and leaking, you will have to find an alternate source of drinking water.
4. Recover supplies from the ship's emergency survival equipment storage, located in the black box above ship's power. Available supplies include:
  a. Multipurpose wrench
  b. Basic particulate sieve
  c. Emergency firearm
  d. Emergency battery pack
  e. Portable assembly unit
  f. MAT input interface
5. Refer back to the MAT unit when complete. The replicator should be able to provide some bottles and some water. It has taken damage but appears to just barely be functional.
6. Proceed to the next available survival task. Consult your MAT unit regularly for recommended tasks and adaptive advice for your continued survival.

If you are having issues surviving your first night, it may help you to make a trench around the ship. Use the dust you get to build a 2 block wall on the inside of the trench. That should keep you safe from everything but spiders. To deal with them, make a small overhang out of stone or wood when you can afford it.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.easy_route.name: The Easy Route
hqm.quest.basic_survival.easy_route.desc:
In case of crash landing, you were equipped with a deluxe survival package:
- Sync Shell Constructor
- Spare Power Cell
- Extra Shotgun Shells
- Saplings
- Fertiliser
- Water Bottles
- Dried Nutrient Bricks
- Choice of Sandwich
Note: Choose this for an easier experience. Completing this quest disables the hard route quest.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.easy_route.task: Check the box below to confirm you want to take the Easy Route with the deluxe survival package. \u00A7oThis is irreversible!\u00A7r
hqm.quest.basic_survival.hard_route.name: The Hard Route
hqm.quest.basic_survival.hard_route.desc:
In case of crash landing, you were equipped with a basic survival package:
- Saplings
- Fertiliser
- Water Bottles
- Dried Nutrient Bricks
Note: Choose this path if you want a challenge. Don't expect to live. Completing this quest disables the easy route quest.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.hard_route.task: Check the box below to confirm you want to take the Hard Route with the basic survival package. \u00A7oThis is irreversible!\u00A7r
hqm.quest.basic_survival.basic_sifting.d: The fertiliser in your survival package will not last long. Place the mesh in the sieve and sift some dust to get bone meal.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.basic_sifting.t: If you want to sift faster, you can place sieves next to one another, allowing multiple to be sifted at once. Alternatively, a compressed sieve takes up just one block and can sift compressed dust.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.furnace.name: Fired Up
hqm.quest.basic_survival.furnace.desc: Despite the planet's high temperature, it isn't nearly hot enough cook food or melt metals. For that, you will need a furnace.
You can get cobblestone by sieving dust or dirt for stone pebbles. Alternatively, with some careful planning, you may be able to generate cobblestone by connecting the water leak on the back of the ship to the fuel leak from the detached reactor. Once you have a source of stone, you can use it to craft your furnace and start smelting.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.basic_metals.de: What Talos lacks in water, it makes up for in metals. If you spend some time sifting, you should be able to get enough metal to set up some infrastructure.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.basic_metals.ta: Sifting dust and other blocks will drop metal ore chunks. Those can be crafted into ores and then smelted into ingots.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.crucible.name: Melting Pot
hqm.quest.basic_survival.crucible.desc: With a furnace set up, you can take the next step. Check the port engine, where the water reclamation system has leaked and turned some of the dust to clay. Dig that up, make a crucible, and place it above a torch or some lava. In the crucible, not only can you melt cobblestone into lava, but you can melt down ore and ore chunks into molten metal. All you need is a casting table to cast the molten metal into ingots. If you ever need more clay, it can be made from water and dust in a barrel.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.crucible.task.0: The crucible can be used to melt ores as well as stone, functioning as a mini-smeltery. Shift-right-click to place a faucet. It can accept ore blocks or chunks. If you've still have lava by the broken engine, you can use that to heat your crucible. Also, you can make casts by pouring gold over wood tool parts.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.flint_mesh.name: Fine-Toothed Comb
hqm.quest.basic_survival.flint_mesh.desc: String mesh can be upgraded to flint mesh to gain higher yields. It can be further upgraded later when you get the resources. Each mesh tier is better than the last.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.flint_mesh.task: You can get flint from sifting gravel, which can be crushed from cobblestone with a hammer or found by digging underground.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.advanced_metals: Uncommon metals and crystals can be found by sifting sand, gravel, and crushed deepslate.

Sifting dust drops iron, copper, gold, and redstone.
Sifting sand drops iron, tin, zinc, nickel, quartz, and certus quartz.
Sifting gravel drops iron, copper, gold, tin, zinc, nickel, lead, silver, coal, and redstone
Sifting crushed deepslate drops iron, copper, gold, silver, lead, redstone, lapis, diamonds, and emeralds.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.centrifuge_wate: Another way to get water is to drop some saplings or leaves into the Centrifugal Separator. It will give you a bit of water. Remember, you can power your machines with the flux capacitor from your emergency supply chest.
Make sure you don't use up all of your saplings, the only way to get more is from leaves or sifting dirt.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.barrel_dirt.des: For your continued survival, you'll need to start farming crops and trees on a larger scale. Neither of those are able to take root in the dust of this planet. However, you can compost organic material in a barrel to make some more dirt for yourself.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.barrel_dirt.tas: Make a barrel with some planks and a slab, then drop some leaves or saplings into it to start composting it into dirt. You'll be farming in no time.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.dirty_water.des: Water is scarce on this planet. If you get desperate enough, you can squeeze the liquid out of some dirt for some very dirty water. Make sure not to use up all your dirt though, you'll need it for growing trees and crops.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.dirty_water.tas: Craft an empty bottle and dirt together to get dirty water.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.acceptable_wate: Dirty water may help you in a pinch, but for long term survival, you'll need to purify it.

The easiest way to purify water is with some fire. Put a dirty water bottle into a furnace, apply some heat, and you'll get clean, drinkable water. You can also make acceptable water directly by melting organic matter.
Purifying using with fire can provide a lot of clean water, but it works slowly. For a faster and more portable method, you can craft water filters.
Water filters can be crafted with water bottles or buckets to purify them by one level.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.camel_pack.name: The Last Straw
hqm.quest.basic_survival.camel_pack.desc: Desert survivors have long made use of portable water reservoirs for hydration. The most useful of which include a built-in straw that connects to the wearer's mouth, allowing them to drink whenever they would like.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.camel_pack.task: Camel packs can be filled with liquid to passively provide hydration. The attached tank can be filled from most tank blocks, or by crafting together with bottles and buckets. The filter helps to automatically purify most water, but when crafting, you must use bottles with a purity of Acceptable or Purified. Camel packs can be upgraded to get higher capacity, and eventually to absorb water directly from the air.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.paste.name: Cut and Paste
hqm.quest.basic_survival.paste.desc: If you need to glue something in a pinch, you don't need to find slime to do it. It turns out mixing water and flour makes a great adhesive.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.paste.task.0.lo: Craft some water and wheat together to make paste, a sticky substance that can be used in many recipes instead of slimeballs.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.rich_soil.name: Fertile Ground
hqm.quest.basic_survival.rich_soil.desc: You should be able to make more fertile soil by mixing some compostable materials into dirt and letting it sit for a few days. When ready, it can be tilled and used like normal farmland, but anything planted in it will grow faster.
Mixing some compostable materials into dirt will make organic compost.
Organic compost will turn into rich soil if left out for a while. If you place it in sunlight, near water, and/or near mushroom blocks, the process will speed up.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.soul_sand.name: Old Soul
hqm.quest.basic_survival.soul_sand.desc: The harsh reality is that you're stuck on this planet. No amount of obsidian rectangles will let you escape. However, the situation means you can't get some resources (like soul sand) through normal methods.
To start, you'll have to sift some dirt, probably a lot of it. Eventually you'll find some mycelium spores. Plant the spores on a piece of dirt and you'll get mycelium.
Placing some mycelium under a barrel full of water will slowly convert it into Witch Water. Put some sand in a barrel of Witch Water and it will turn into soul sand.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.netherrack_end_: This world doesn't have any lava lakes or dragons, so you'll have to get some materials in other ways. A barrel full of lava can be turned into netherrack or end stone using redstone or glowstone respectively.

Place a barrel down, fill it with lava, and click it with redstone or glowstone. Make sure to use a stone barrel, or you risk spreading lava everywhere. When you get access to advanced melting, you can make netherrack and end stone with an extruder and some liquid redstone or ender pearls.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.tinker_tables.d: A finely crafted weapon or tool isn't as easy as strapping some rocks to a stick. In fact, basic tools like that won't work for you at all. You'll have to tinker around a bit.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.tinker_tables.t: First, make a part builder and a tinker station. The part builder lets you make parts by combining a pattern and a material. The tinker station lets you assemble parts into tools.
Every tool needs a handle, a wood handle should do the trick. You can make one by putting some wood in the part builder with a pattern.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.crook.name: By Hook or by Crook
hqm.quest.basic_survival.crook.desc: Breaking leaves will give saplings, but the drop chance is low. By knocking them down with a crook, you can triple your chance of finding saplings. Perhaps you can find something else useful in the leaves as well.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.crook.task.0.lo: A crook will increase the drop chance of saplings from leaves, and has a small chance of giving a silk worm. Crooks are crafted from sticks or in a tinker station.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.string.name: String Theory
hqm.quest.basic_survival.string.desc: Silk worms can be found in tree leaves, and under certain conditions, they will spread through a tree, spinning cocoons of usable silk.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.string.task.0.l: Right-click some leaves with a silk worm to infest them. Infested leaf blocks will drop string and more silk worms, and the silk worms will spread to adjacent leaf blocks. This is useful for getting string. Break the infested leaves with a crook for higher yields.
Desert planet inhabitants have developed effective clothes that can help you stay cool in the blazing heat. These clothes provide insulation from outside temperatures but can also allow enough airflow to let off body heat when it's cooler than you are. They also provide high coverage, protecting you from the sun's rays.

Desert Armour provides excellent heat protection properties. It is mostly made from leather and string. Leather can be gained by cooking rotten flesh and string can be gained from silkworm-infested leaves.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.leather_insulat: Desert clothing is useful for protection, but it's bulky and doesn't allow you to wear armor with it. One alternative is to put a thin layer of insulating material between you and your armor. This isn't usually as effective, but it allows for more protection from attack.
Insulation items can be placed in the curios Insulation slot, and provide smaller amounts of protection from the heat, but allowing armor to be worn at the same time.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.stillsuit.name: Swimming in Strange Water
hqm.quest.basic_survival.stillsuit.desc: The sun's scorching heat is often only bearable from within shelter. However, there are tales of survivors that can spend weeks on end in deathly heat using special suits. These stillsuits encase someone completely, recapturing lost water and using it to both regulate temperature and for drinking.
The stillsuit provides more protection from the elements than any other type of insulation, and halves the wearer's water consumption rate.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.mattock.name: Breaking New Ground
hqm.quest.basic_survival.mattock.desc: You'll need some tools to stay alive out here as well. Bone tools are likely the best starting material, but you can make a different type if you'd like. Wood and stone tools are generally ineffective.
You can make a mattock with the axe and adze heads, it will be an essential tool for farming early on. Eventually you may want a pickaxe and some other tools, but farming food is vital for your survival, and the mattock can help mine logs and dust as well.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.sword.name: Live to Fight Another Day
hqm.quest.basic_survival.sword.desc: The night is dark and full of terrors. Your chances of survival are low, but you can improve them with some sort of weapon to defend yourself.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.sword.task.0.lo: Weapon blades can be made from a variety of materials, though bone blades are usually the strongest when starting out. Bone tool parts can be made from bones or bone meal in a part builder.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.hammer.name: Hammer Time
hqm.quest.basic_survival.hammer.desc: The surface of Talos is covered in siftable dust, and sand, gravel, and crushed deepslate can be found underground for sifting. These blocks can also be made by crushing other blocks with a hammer. Hammers can be used to crush cobblestone into gravel, gravel into sand, and sand into dust.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.hammer.task.0.l: A hammer can crush stone into gravel and sand. It can be made as a tinker tool.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.hammer.task.1.l: Break cobblestone with a hammer to get gravel, and break gravel to get sand. You can generate cobblestone where flowing water and lava meet. The water and fuel leaks near the back of the ship could be connected for an early source of stone.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.mob_drops.name: The Night Shift
hqm.quest.basic_survival.mob_drops.desc: The "life" on Talos seems to mostly be made up of the animated bodies of its former inhabitants, all of which appear hostile. The optimal survival strategy is to avoid confrontation, but some of them leave behind useful items when killed.
Kill mobs to collect their drops. Rotten flesh can be used for zombie jerky or smelted into leather. Bones can be used as an early tool material or to make bone meal for crops. Spider eyes can be used to make soup in a pinch, and gunpowder can make all sorts of explosives.
The most interesting mob drop is the ender pearl. Not only can it teleport the player when thrown, but its teleportation-related properties allow all sorts of interesting items to be crafted from it.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.shell_construct: This planet is full of hazards and hostiles. You will eventually need to venture out of the confines of your ship, but that poses a lot of risks. However, with a bit of effort, you may be able to give yourself a second chance if the worst happens. A Shell Constructor is the key to life after (first) death. Once you make one, you will need to provide energy and a blood sample and it will build you a new body.
Place the constructor, give it a power source, and right-click it to provide the DNA sample. Be careful, it will hurt a little.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.shell_storage.d: Sometimes, one life just isn't enough. In those cases, you can use Shell Storage to keep extra shells around. When you die, you will be sent to a random shell.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.shell_storage.t: If you have another shell available, you can put your current body into storage. Just walk into the shell storage chamber and it will let you transfer to any available Shell.

Some important warnings:

1. When you enter storage to switch shells, your items stay in that body. Empty your inventory before syncing unless you have multiple Shell Storage chambers available.
2. If a Shell Storage breaks, the Shell it is storing will be lost and its inventory will be scattered on the ground.

Check the box below to acknowledge the Sync™ terms and conditions.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.easy_route_trig: Invisible trigger quest to control quests unlocked by the easy route
hqm.quest.basic_survival.pressed_metal_t: Invisible trigger quest for when the player unlocks the press.
hqm.quest.basic_survival.alloying_trigge: Invisible trigger quest for when the player unlocks an alloying method.
hqm.quest_set.the_food_pyramid.desc: Guide to acquiring and cooking food from the resources available on the planet.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.grains.name: Against the Grain
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.grains.desc: You'll need to maintain a balanced diet to survive without negative effects. Finding a reliable source of grains is the most urgent part of that since they decay faster than most nutrients. \u00A7lGrains affect your movement, mining, and attack speed\u00A7r.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.grains.task.0: Wheat and rice are the primary grains, used for bread, sandwiches, sweets, and a variety of meals. Wheat seeds and rice can be found by sifting dirt. Rice must be planted in a water source block to grow, making it more difficult to farm at scale.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.proteins.name: Magic Beans
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.proteins.desc: Proteins are the next most important part of a balanced diet since they decay moderately fast. \u00A7lProteins affect your attack strength\u00A7r.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.proteins.task: Beans and peanuts are the primary plant-based proteins. They can be used for soups, sandwiches, sweets, and more. Both have a chance of dropping from sifting dirt, or can be found in abandoned farm houses.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.vegetables.de: Vegetables are another important part of your balanced diet, though they decay fairly slowly. \u00A7lVegetables affect your resistance to damage\u00A7r.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.vegetables.ta: There are a large variety of vegetables to choose from for your meals, and are essential for many dishes. Each vegetable seed has a small chance of dropping from sifting dirt, or can be found in abandoned farm houses.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.fruits.name: Fruits of Your Labour
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.fruits.desc: Fruits are another important part of your balanced diet. \u00A7lFruits affect your health regeneration speed\u00A7r.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.fruits.task.0:
There are three main fruits to farm; apples, sweet berries, and melons. Additionally, tomatoes are considered both a fruit and a vegetable.
Apples drop from oak leaves, while sweet berries and melon seeds have a small chance of dropping from sifting dirt, or can be found in abandoned farm houses.
Apples are easier to obtain in small quantities, but sweet berries are the easiest to farm when you need a more permanent source of fruits.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.sugars.name: Sugarcoating It
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.sugars.desc: Sugars aren't necessary for a balanced diet but they can be useful for energy when you need it. Small amounts can speed you up, but \u00A74too much sugar will give negative effects\u00A7r.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.sugars.task.0: Sugar can be made from sugarcane, which can be gained from sifting dirt.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.bread.name: Breaking Bread
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.bread.desc: Not only is bread an incredibly simple dietary staple, but it can be crafted into a variety of other useful meals.
Bread can be made from three wheat. Once you get access to crushing tools, you can make bread more efficiently from wheat flour.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.beans_and_ric: Beans and rice are a very simple to make but very nutritious dish.
Beans and rice can be made from beans and rice (unsurprisingly), cooked together in a pot.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.peanut_butter: PB&Js are an easy-to-make and nutritious classic.
Peanut butter is made from peanuts, bread from wheat, and your choice of fruit.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.pasta_and_tom: Pasta and Tomato Sauce is a quick source of multiple food groups.
Pasta is made from dough, which is made from wheat and water. Tomato sauce is made from 2 tomatoes. This creates a simple, 2-ingredient dish.
Talos seems to entirely lack plant life, which does not leave much to eat once your rations run out. As a temporary solution, you may have to sustain yourself with the flesh scavenged from the undead that emerge at night.
The dust on Talos has a high salt concentration. Salt can be used to cure and preserve food, rendering it safe for consumption. Sift some dust to collect salt.
The zombies that hunt at night seem to burn up every morning, leaving their flesh behind. If you're careful, you could collect some of it, but watch out for any creatures that didn't burn up.

Combining a piece of rotten flesh with some salt will make something edible. It is not a strong source of nutrition, but it is far less poisonous than normal rotten flesh and should be suitable until better food can be found.
Zombie jerky is a poor long-term food source. However, you don't have many options at the moment. To add a bit of variety to your diet, you can craft some food out of other mob drops.
Monster mash is made by mixing together rotten flesh, bones, and salt.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.bug_broth.des: Monster mash leaves a lot to be desired. Perhaps cooking some monster parts into a soup will make them taste a bit better, if you can ignore what it's made of.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.bug_broth.tas: Bug broth is made by mixing together some salt and bug parts in a cooking pot.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.enderios.name: Pearl Jam
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.enderios.desc: The ender pearl is a fascinating material with interesting properties. It seems like it could be turned into viable food source if neutralised with some gunpowder. Be careful though, as there may be some strange side effects from eating it.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.enderios.task: Enderios are made by mixing together ender pearl dust, wheat, and gunpowder in a cooking pot.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.cooking_pot.d: Your starting food will only last a few days, so you're in dire need of a food source. If you make a cooking pot, you'll be able to prepare a wider variety of nutritional foods.
hqm.quest.the_food_pyramid.cooking_pot.t: A cooking pot must be placed above a fire source to cook. The easiest fire source to manage is a campfire. Place a campfire in the ground with the cooking pot on top and you'll be making meals in no time! (Be careful not to get too close to the flame or you risk burning yourself!)
Getting a food source is urgent, but crops grow slowly. The fertiliser in your survival package won't last very long, so investing in another way to speed up crop growth is a good idea.

The watering can speeds up plant growth when used on crops. It can be upgraded to increase its capacity and range. Advanced watering cans will no longer consume water once they have been filled all the way for the first time.
hqm.quest_set.like_clockwork.desc: Guide to setting up rotational force-based automation with minimal resources.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.simple_create.d: The MAT unit is capable of providing a simple guide to creating mechanical contraptions using rotational force, but also has a more comprehensive guide that can be opted-into instead. \u00A7lThis is irreversible!\u00A7r
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.simple_create.t: Most of the Create mod is not required to complete this modpack. If you want to skip the guide to Create and just play with the 6 most relevant quests, click the checkbox below. If not, complete the "Full Steam Ahead" quest instead.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.detailed_create: The MAT unit is capable of providing a comprehensive guide to creating mechanical contraptions using rotational force, but also has an abbreviated guide that can be opted-into instead. \u00A7lThis is irreversible!\u00A7r

Most of the Create mod is not required to complete this modpack. If you want the full guide to Create with 30+ quests, click the checkbox below. If not, complete the "Down to Brass Tacks" quest instead.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.andesite_alloy_: You'll need some basic building blocks before you can start setting up machinery.

Andesite alloy is used for simple machines and serves as a building block for all sorts of moving parts. It is made from andesite and iron or zinc nuggets. Remember, andesite can be crafted from cobblestone and any type of quartz.

Shafts are made from andesite alloy and serve as a simple rotating part that other machines can connect to.

Andesite casing can be used to make basic machinery. It is made by right-clicking a stripped wood log with andesite alloy.
