hqm.quest.like_clockwork.hand_crank.name: Getting a Handle on Things
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.hand_crank.desc: Rotational force is a simple method of conveying energy for automation before electricity becomes a viable alternative. One of the easiest methods of creating rotational energy is manually turning a crank.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.hand_crank.task: The hand crank produces a small amount of rotational force when operated. By holding right-click, the crank rotates anticlockwise, and using shift + right-click reverses the direction. Each use spins the crank at 32 RPM for approximately 0.5 seconds, delivering a 90° rotation to any directly connected mechanical bearing with a 1:1 ratio. However, using the crank will consume your hunger, making it a limited, albeit simple, power source. To make it, all you will need is three planks and an andesite alloy.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.windmill.name: Wind in Your Sails
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.windmill.desc: Rotational force is a simple method of conveying energy for automation before electricity becomes a viable alternative. One of the most effective methods of harnessing natural rotational energy is harnessing the energy of the wind.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.windmill.task.0: A windmill is an automatic power generator that produces rotational force using a windmill bearing and at least eight sail-type blocks, such as windmill sails, sail frames, or wool blocks. To construct a windmill, attach any block to the Windmill Bearing's sticky side, which comes pre-glued for convenience, and then connect sail-type blocks to the hub block you just placed. The windmill becomes functional once it has at least eight sail blocks, generating 1 RPM and 512 stress units (SU) for every increment of eight sails, up to a maximum of 8192 SU at 128 sails. The orientation of the sails doesn't affect performance; they can be placed in any shape or pattern. You can start or stop the windmill by right-clicking the bearing with an empty hand and can change its spin direction by interacting with the centre of the bearing. By default, the windmill spins clockwise, but this can be reversed using a wrench.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.water_wheel.des: Rotational force is a simple method of conveying energy for automation before electricity becomes a viable alternative. One of the simplest methods of harnessing natural rotational energy is harnessing the energy of flowing water.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.water_wheel.tas: The water wheel is a simple power generator that produces rotational force when water flows around it. Place the water wheel into flowing water and it will produce rotational force. Multiple water wheels can be lined up to increase load making it an easy way to generate larger amounts of power.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.belts_funnels.d: Item transportation is vital for automation, and conveyor belts are a simple way to use rotational force to move things from one point to another.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.belts_funnels.t:
To place a belt, you must have at least two shafts facing the same direction; simply right-click one shaft and then the other. A single Mechanical Belt item is used regardless of the distance, provided the length is under 20 blocks. Belts can be placed in straight lines or horizontally, vertically, or diagonally (at a 45° incline), so long as there are no obstructions.
You can extend or shorten belts by right-clicking with a belt or a wrench, which will also reposition the shaft. In addition to transmitting identical rotational force across all connected shafts (as long as the input force is consistent), the mechanical belt excels at moving items and entities. Items can be added by dropping them manually or through machines like funnels, chutes, and mechanical arms, and they can also be removed using similar methods. Belts cannot transport items vertically. If you are wearing diving boots or crouching, you will not be moved by belts. Belts also interact with a variety of machines: mechanical presses can press items passing underneath, deployers can interact with items on the belt, spouts can fill them with liquids, and encased fans can perform bulk processing like washing or smelting. Brass Tunnels help with item sorting and organization, whilst Depots can act as temporary stops for other machines to interact with items. For added customization, belts can be dyed with any dye, adding coloured stripes, and the dye can be removed with a water bucket or bottle.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.cogwheel.name: Gearing Up
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.cogwheel.desc: Cogwheels can be used to extend rotational force perpendicular to a shaft, or to change the direction of rotation. Combining small and large cogwheels also allows rotation speed to be increased or decreased.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.cogwheel.task.0: Cogwheels transmit and manipulate rotational force. The basic Cogwheel and its larger variant, the Large Cogwheel, allow for various interlocking configurations that control the direction, speed, and axis of rotational force. When two cogwheels are placed side-by-side and face the same direction, they rotate in opposite directions at equal speeds. Two large cogwheels interlock when placed perpendicularly, changing the rotational axis without affecting speed. A cogwheel and a large cogwheel interlock diagonally, with the cogwheel rotating at twice the speed of the larger one. Cogwheels can also act like shafts, transmitting rotation from both ends unless encased, and multiple cogwheels connected in a line function like a series of shafts. Cogwheels are also used to activate certain blocks; if a block features a cogwheel in its texture, it can be powered by placing a cogwheel directly next to it or a large cogwheel diagonally, provided they're aligned in the same direction.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.gearbox.name: Shifting Gears
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.gearbox.desc: Cogs take up a lot of space, and sometimes a simple change in direction is all you need. Gearboxes can provide that in a small space.
The gearbox distributes rotational power in multiple directions, either horizontally or vertically, depending on its orientation. When powered from any of its input sides, it relays rotation to the other three output sides. The key behaviour of the gearbox is that it inverts the rotational direction: if the input rotation is clockwise, the outputs will rotate anticlockwise, and vice versa. This makes it particularly useful for splitting power between multiple machines or systems whilst maintaining synchronised but opposite motion across different components. The vertical variant functions the same way but distributes power along the vertical axis.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.millstone.name: The Daily Grind
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.millstone.desc: The millstone can grind small items into dusts, useful for ore processing, making flour, and a variety of other applications where grinding something up is useful.
The millstone is a processing machine and a simpler version of the more advanced crushing wheels. It performs milling recipes on valid items inserted from above. It can be powered either from below via a shaft or from the side using a cogwheel. Items can be fed into the Millstone either by dropping them directly on top or by using hoppers, funnels, chutes, or other item transport systems. However, it does not automatically output processed items; you must either right-click the machine with an empty hand or use an external extractor like a Hopper or Funnel to retrieve the output. To get a full list of all millstone recipes, consult the JEI.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.mechanical_pres: Forming metal into thin sheets is vital for making more advanced contraptions. A mechanical press can do just that.

The humble Mechanical Press can press and pack items below it. Simply place the press with one block of space between it and the ground and throw your items underneath and apply power! Note that it processes items faster when it receives faster rotational power.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.mechanical_extr: Cobblestone can be generated by casting water and lava together, but that takes up a lot of space and likely violates some industrial safety procedures. It's possible to fit the main press and mining equipment in a small space.

The mechanical extruder is used to automate the production of stone-type blocks. When powered with rotational force as well as having the necessary liquid source blocks adjacent to its sides, the mechanical extruder can create cobblestone, scoria, stone, basalt, or limestone. The block underneath the extruder does matter in some cases of production (see JEI for details). The blocks it produces can be extracted either with a right-click or automatically pulled out with a combination of a funnel and moving belt.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.iron_sheet.name: Pumping Iron
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.iron_sheet.desc: Iron plating is typically used for moving parts and machines of intermediate complexity.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.iron_sheet.task: Iron plates are made from putting iron ingots into a mechanical press.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.super_glue.name: Holding it Together
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.super_glue.desc: To set up complicated contraptions full of moving parts, you'll need a way to make sure everything stays attached.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.super_glue.task: Super Glue binds blocks together in moving contraptions, ensuring they act as a single structure during motion. Each use reduces the glue's durability by one, although enchantments like Unbreaking and Mending can prolong its lifespan. In Block by Block Mode, glue is applied by right-clicking the face of a chassis or held in the off-hand to automatically apply glue whilst placing blocks. This method mimics the use of a Slimeball but allows for more flexible attachment, including placing blocks on chassis edges. Glue applied this way is permanent unless manually removed by sneak right-clicking with an empty hand. Area Mode allows you to glue multiple blocks after placement by selecting a 3D section. This is done by right-clicking one corner and then the opposite corner of a region, up to 24 blocks apart. Hold the super glue in your main hand to visually identify glued blocks with green outlines, though glue applied directly to surfaces won’t show these outlines unless placed with the glue in the offhand. Left-click with super glue on green areas to remove the glue.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.chute.name: Drop Zone
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.chute.desc: Where belts are used for horizontal item transportation, Chutes are design for vertical item transportation.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.chute.task.0.lo: Chutes function similarly to mechanical belts but are designed for moving items up or down directly. They can both insert into and extract from inventories positioned directly above or below, and when connected vertically or diagonally, they automatically pass items between each other. By default, items fall through chutes due to gravity, but upward movement is possible using encased fans positioned either above (to pull) or below (to push), with fan speed determining the rate of item transport. Chutes also support complex logistics through merging and splitting. Multiple chute lines can converge, though items won't combine into single stacks. In fan-powered setups, item routing follows basic preferences: pushing fans prioritise straight paths, whilst pulling fans draw items towards themselves. Speed and airflow efficiency are affected by how chutes are connected. Aesthetically, chutes can be modified: right-clicking with a wrench adds windows, and non-diagonal chutes can be visually upgraded by encasing them with industrial iron blocks.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.mechanical_mixe: A mechanical mixer can be used to mix batches of items together, and it can be heated for melting, cooking, and alloying.

The Mechanical Mixer is a mechanical component that processes Mixing recipes and shapeless crafting recipes in a Basin. It requires at least 30 RPM to function, with higher speeds improving efficiency. The Mixer must be placed above a Basin with a 1-block gap to work.

Automation: Can automate shapeless crafting by inserting ingredients into the Basin.

Brewing: Can automate Brewing recipes when combined with a heated Blaze Burner.

Mixing: Some recipes (e.g., Brass) require a super-heated Blaze Burner.

The Mixer acts as a cogwheel, transmitting and reversing rotation to adjacent components.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.mechanical_saw_: With moving parts, a variety of farming contraptions can be made to automatically harvest blocks. Harvesters can be used to harvest crops, saws can be used to chop trees, and drills can be used for any other block.

The Mechanical Saw cuts wood blocks in front of it and can automatically fell entire trees or giant mushrooms by breaking the bottom-most block. It can fully cut down 2x2 trees if at least one bottom block is mined. Saws damage entities and break blocks based on contraption speed. When placed facing upward, the saw applies stonecutting recipes, selecting a random output unless a filter is used. You can also use them to create more shafts per andesite alloy than standard crafting.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.encased_fan.des: The encased fan can blow air to push items on the ground, and it can blow water, fire, and lava to wash or cook things.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.encased_fan.tas: The Encased Fan can create air streams to pull or push entities or items. This works vertically and horizontally and the strength is directly correlated to rotational speed. The Encased fan also has the ability to do Bulk Washing, Bulk Blasting, Bulk Haunting, and Bulk Smoking.

Bulk Washing requires water to be placed directly in front of the fan's airstream or at the end if the fan is pulling air. Throw your items into the stream to start washing. Throw some sand into the stream and get yourself some clay!

Bulk Blasting requires lava to be placed directly in front of the fan's airstream or at the end if the fan is pulling air. This works like a blast furnace but can destroy items if they cant be blasted! Know that it cannot process Ore blocks and will destroy them. Try making some charcoal by throwing wood into the stream!
Bulk Smoking requires a campfire to be placed directly in front of the fan's airstream or at the end if the fan is pulling air. Try making some leather by throwing rotten flesh into the stream!

Bulk Haunting requires a soul campfire or flame to be placed directly in front of the fan's airstream or at the end if the fan is pulling air. This has a number of special uses including acquiring nether blocks.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.blaze_burner.de: A Blaze Burner can be used to provide heat for mixing items in the basin, or as a heat source for the crucible.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.blaze_burner.ta:
An Empty Blaze Burner is the unfilled version of a Blaze Burner and must be filled with a Blaze to function further. To capture a Blaze, simply right-click a Blaze or Blaze spawner whilst holding an Empty Blaze Burner. This will not damage the spawner.

Without the Blaze, it can be used as a Soul Fire Burner with Soul Sand or Soul Soil, serving as a passive boiler heat source and for Bulk Smoking or Bulk Haunting, but not for Mixing.

A filled Blaze Burner allows you to make brass, and provide heat for Steam Engines, contributing 1 heating level in the Heated phase and 2 in the Super-Heated phase. It is also used for Bulk Smoking and Bulk Smelting when fueled. Blaze Burners can be powered by burnable items, and Deployers or Mechanical Arms can automate fueling, ensuring efficient use of resources. For extra style, throw some engineer's goggles on the Blaze Burner.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.copper_sheet.de: Copper plating is often used in fluid transportation.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.copper_sheet.ta: Copper plates are made from putting copper ingots into a mechanical press.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.spout.name: Ebb and Flow
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.spout.desc: The Spout is used to fill liquid containers or craft with liquids.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.spout.task.0.lo:
The Spout dispenses fluid onto items passing below it on a Conveyor Belt or Depot. Each item takes 1 second to process, though refill time may cause slight delays. The Spout holds up to 1 bucket of a single liquid, which is supplied via Fluid Pipes.

The Depot serves as a machine interaction point, allowing items to be placed manually or inserted automatically. Machines like the Mechanical Arm or Mechanical Press can interact with items on the Depot, just as they would on a Mechanical Belt. Items on a Depot do not despawn and remain until removed by a player or another machine.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.item_drain.name: Down the Drain
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.item_drain.desc: The Item Drain extracts liquids from bottles, buckets, and other fluid containers.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.item_drain.task: The Item Drain can hold up to 1500 mB of liquid and requires a Fluid Pump to extract fluids. Basins will automatically deposit output fluids into a nearby Item Drain.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.golden_sheet.de: Gold plating is often used in personal equipment.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.golden_sheet.ta: Gold plates are made from putting gold ingots into a mechanical press.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.engineers_goggl: Engineer's Goggles provide detailed analysis of a machine's rotational speed and stress level at a glance.

A wearable item that displays machine details, including stress impact, rotation speed, and fluid levels in tanks. When worn, it provides enhanced visual feedback for Stressometers and Speedometers. Compatible with Curios/Trinkets mods for alternate head slot usage.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.wrench.name: A Wrench in the Works
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.wrench.desc: The Wrench is a versatile tool for rotating, dismantling, and configuring components.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.wrench.task.0.l: Right-click rotates a component, whilst Shift + Right-click dismantles it. Scroll over certain components to configure them, and hold Ctrl to configure all connected components at once.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.brass_sheet.des: Brass plating is often used for advanced machinery, and electron tubing enables some "smart" features.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.brass_sheet.tas: Brass plates are made from putting brass ingots into a mechanical press, and electron tubes are made from polished rose quartz. Rose quartz is crafted from quartz and redstone, which can be polished by using sandpaper whilst the rose quartz is in your offhand.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.mechanical_craf: The Mechanical Crafter is a machine that crafts items when powered by rotational force.

The connection between Mechanical Crafters is established through the path indicated by the block's design. To change the direction it sends items during crafting, simply right-click the front of the crafter with a Wrench. In a setup, the crafters can be automatically filled by Funnels or Hoppers, and they can share inventories without being part of the same crafting recipe. A Wrench can also be used on the back and sides of Mechanical Crafters to connect or disconnect adjacent crafters' inventories. Items can be manually inserted or removed as well.

Each Mechanical Crafter requires rotational power from either adjacent crafters or any size Cogwheel. This means that only one crafter in a setup needs to be powered by a Cogwheel for the entire system to work. Once powered, and when all the crafting slots are filled or a redstone signal is received, the Mechanical Crafters will send their items to adjacent crafters. To successfully craft an item, the components must eventually meet in one crafter, where they will turn into the final product. Crafter Slot Covers can act as empty spaces in a recipe, allowing for the connection of separate crafters, but they do not move the items themselves.

If the items do not form a valid recipe, the crafters will eject the items instead of crafting the product. For automating crafting, directly adjacent slots can be merged to hold a single item type, like andesite alloy. This allows the material to be fed in from the side via a hopper, streamlining the crafting process. Powered Mechanical Crafters will start crafting once all slots are filled or when a redstone signal is applied.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.crushing_wheels: Crushing Wheels are an advanced version of Millstones that are more powerful, and can crush a greater variety of items than the Millstone, and sometimes with higher yields.

Crushing Wheels crush items inserted from the direction they are spinning away from. To function, two Crushing Wheels must be placed next to each other, either horizontally or vertically, one block apart, with opposite rotational forces. Items to be crushed should be inserted where the wheels rotate inwards. Automation is possible by placing a hopper between the wheels and connecting it to a depot or conveyor belt below.
The Electric Motor converts electricity to rotational force, and the Alternator converts rotational force into energy

The electric motor is useful compared to other sources of rotational force because of how compact and adjustable it is. Note that the higher the RPM is set, the more energy will be used to power it. Simply power the electric motor from the opposing side of its shaft to get instant rotational force.

The alternator requires a minimum of 32 RPM to operate. Energy production is linear with RPM: the higher the RPM, the more energy will be produced. Connect the opposing side to the shaft to any power source or cable to collect energy to be used or stored.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.deployer.name: Helping Hand
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.deployer.desc: The deployer has a mechanical hand, designed to use items just like a person would. It can be set to use tools, interact with blocks, and even attack.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.deployer.task.0: The Deployer is a machine that can be given items either directly or by right-clicking them into its hand. It can be stopped with a redstone signal and has a filter on its side to control which items it uses, which is especially important when using the Deployer in a Contraption. The Deployer has two inventory slots: one for the held item and another for extra items, such as those harvested by the Deployer. These harvested items are transferred to the extra slot and must be removed by machines, during which the Deployer will stall. Items in the extra slot cannot be extracted directly by the player. By default, the Deployer simulates right-clicks, but it can be switched to left-click mode by right-clicking the front with a Wrench. In left-click mode, the Deployer can use tools like pickaxes and swords, mimicking the player's actions, including causing mobs to drop rare items when slain.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.precision_mecha: The Precision Mechanism is an intricate component for more complex devices.

To make a Precision Mechanism, send a golden sheet through a factory line and deploy a small cogwheel, large cogwheel, and then an iron nugget to the sheet. Repeat this process to create the mechanism. However, due to the complexity of the device, there is a 20% chance of failure, where all you get back is scrap.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.rotation_speed_: The Rotation Speed Controller is used to precisely control rotational speed instead of requiring a large gear shifting contraption.

The Rotation Speed Controller adjusts the speed of whatever source of rotational force is provided as input, and outputs through a cogwheel, which is placed on top. The rotation speed and direction can be adjusted in the Value Settings Screen located on the front or back of the controller. The speed can be set to a maximum of 256 RPM.
hqm.quest.like_clockwork.detailed_create: Invisible trigger quest for the player selecting the more detailed Create path.
hqm.quest_set.under_pressure.desc: Guide to pneumatic technologies for manipulating and utilizing compressed air.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.compressed_iron: When you have your basic survival taken care of, you can start developing more advanced technology. The first step of that process will be creating a new kind of metal.
Start by gathering some iron ingots.

Now, you'll need some TNT. You should have the gunpowder by now (either from sifting or from creepers if you're brave). To get sand, break cobblestone with a hammer to make gravel, then break that to make sand.

For the final step, you should move far away from your base. Drop some iron on the ground, place the TNT next to it, ignite the TNT, and then stand far away. When the dust settles, you should have some compressed iron.
With compressed iron, you can start working with compressed air.

The pressure tube is the most basic component for using compressed air. You must use these tubes to transfer the air around. The longer the tubes extend, the more pressure will be lost. Try to keep things close to one another to avoid depressurising. Make sure your pressure tubes don't have any open ends or you will leak a lot of pressure.

The air compressor will generate compressed air when provided with solid fuel. Charcoal is a good starting fuel. Be careful not to generate too much pressure though. Anything over 5 bars of pressure risks an explosion. You can enable and disable the compressor with a redstone signal if you'd like, which can later be automated to automatically turn it off when close to overloading.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.pressure_chambe: Now that you can generate pressurised air, you can start putting it to use. Construct a pressure chamber to start crafting with compressed air.

You can build a 3x3x3 pressure chamber with 1 pressure chamber valve and 25 pressure chamber blocks (either walls or windows). Build a 3x3x3 cube with the centre block missing. One of the blocks adjacent to the centre will be the pressure chamber valve.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.pcb_1_empty_pcb: Now that you have a pressure chamber, you can make all kinds of advanced materials. The most important of these advanced recipes is the Printed Circuit Board, which is an essential component for high-tech crafting. To get started, you'll need some plastic, either refined from oil or melted from scrap found in the ruins.

To start making PCBs, you'll need some plastic. There are a few methods of acquiring it, but it typically involves refining oil or scavenging for plastic scrap in cities. Once you found or made some plastic, you can start making your first PCB.

Once you have the resources, you can start making your first PCB. Use the pressure chamber to combine a piece of plastic with 2 redstone torches and 3 conductive nuggets to get the empty PCB. You will also need 2 capacitors and 2 transistors, which are made from plastic, 3 conductive nuggets, and either an adhesive to make capacitors or redstone dust to make transistors.

To craft using the pressure chamber, break one of the middle blocks, drop your ingredients in, and place the block back down. Once you reach the required pressure level again, your items will be crafted and you can break the block again to remove them from the chamber. You will lose some whenever the pressure chamber is opened, but you can improve upon the process with a pressure chamber interface, which can do the opening/closing for you.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.pcb_2_uv_light_: Once you have an empty PCB, the next step is to expose it to ultraviolet light.
The UV light box is encoded with the blueprint for a PCB. When an empty PCB is placed inside and it is powered by compressed air, the PCB will be exposed to ultraviolet light.

The exposure process will take a long time. You can technically remove the empty PCB from the light box before it is completed, but then it will have chance of failure during the final step. You can install speed upgrades to reduce the wait time or make more machines to speed up bulk processing.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.pcb_3_etching_t: After exposing the empty PCB, you will have to etch the circuit boards with etching acid.
An etching tank is used to etch the PCB with etching acid. The etching acid is made by combining various caustic materials in a pressure chamber.
Place exposed PCBs in an etching tank to etch them. If a PCB is not completely exposed, it has a chance of failure, but failed PCBs can be smelted and exposed again.
The final step of creating a PCB is assembling it.
Simply craft together your unassembled PCB with 2 capacitors and 2 transistors to finish the process.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.gas_lift_oil.de: Subsurface scanning has detected an abundance of oil deep under the surface of the planet. With a bit of pressure, you should be able to pump oil from the depths.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.gas_lift_oil.ta: You'll start with a gas lift and some drill pipes. Provide the gas lift with some pressure and insert the drill pipes, and it will start digging down, automatically placing the pipes as it mines. The deeper it drills, the more drill pipes and pressure it will need. You can reduce this cost by placing your pumps deeper underground.
When your pump reaches the oil at the bottom of the world (roughly 120 metres down), it will start extracting.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.refining_oil.de: Now that you can pump oil out of the depths, you can work on refining it to get plastic, an important resource for making circuits and machinery.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.refining_oil.ta: Put the 4 refinery outputs in a vertical stack above the refinery controller. Use a resistive heater or vortex tube next to the controller to keep it hot enough to run.
When your refinery is running, it will slowly produce refined oils based on how hot the controller is kept.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.plastic_process: Once you have production of refined oil, you can begin to make plastic, a vital ingredient for more advanced manufacturing.
Plastic is made in a Thermopneumatic Processing Plant, by combining LPG and coal using pressure and heat.

The processing plant produces liquid plastic, which can be flash cooled into plastic sheets by dumping the bucket on the ground. For simple automation of this process, you can use a casting table or a blast chiller.
A pressure gauge can measure the amount of pressure in a pneumatic system. With some clever wiring, you can automatically turn off your air compressors when the system has too much pressure.
When placed on a pressure tube, the pressure gauge emits a redstone signal equal to double the detected pressure. You can use that to disable compressors when the system gets close to overloading.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.pressure_chambe: Now that you have a pressure chamber, you'll need a way to put items into it. Technically, you can break one of the blocks and drop the items in manually, but that will vent all of the stored pressure. A better option is the pressure chamber interface, which acts as an airlock, allowing you to insert or extract from the chamber while barely losing any air.

You will need at least two interfaces; one set to input and one set to output. Make sure both are exposed to the air inside the chamber. Once set up, you can use item conduits to move items in and out of the chamber.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.upgrades.name: Better, Faster, Stronger
hqm.quest.under_pressure.upgrades.desc: Many pneumatic machines can have upgrades installed. The most broadly useful one is the speed upgrade, which can increase processing speed in most machines.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.upgrades.task.0: Speed upgrades need lubricant, which is made from diesel and redstone. You'll likely want a lot of it.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.assembly_line.d: Assembling a PCB by hand is extremely time-consuming. Luckily, the process can be simplified when you have the technology. With an assembly line set up, you can automatically handle the etching and exposing to skip right from an empty PCB to an unassembled one.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.assembly_line.t:
1. Place the machines in a square with the two IO units at the top right and top left.
2. Place the laser on the bottom left and the platform to its right.
3. Put a chest adjacent to an IO unit and the assembly controller on any side of the square.
4. Set the output of one of the IO units using a pneumatic wrench.
5. Provide pressurised air for the controller and insert the Assembly Program: Laser.

When the setup is complete, you can place empty PCBs in the chest to process. The input unit will move it to the platform, the laser will etch the PCB pattern onto it, and the output unit will return it to the chest. You can increase the processing speed with speed upgrades.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.misc_tools.name: Tools of the Trade
hqm.quest.under_pressure.misc_tools.desc: There are many useful gadgets you can make using compressed air. You can consult the documentation for the full list, but these are some of the most useful tools.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.misc_tools.task: Many PneumaticCraft gadgets will need to be charged with compressed air before they can be used. Be careful though, the charging station balances air pressure between the item being charged and the rest of the system. If the tool has more bars of pressure than the rest of the network it will actually discharge.

The pneumatic wrench allows rotation of PneumaticCraft blocks and opening/closing pressure tubes by right-clicking, and instant dismantling by shift+right-clicking. It must be charged in a charging station.

Some PneumaticCraft gadgets require selecting specific coordinates to use them. For that, you will need a GPS tool. Right-click on a block to set the tool to those coordinates. Right-click in the air to modify the coordinates. Does not need charging.

The Air Cannon will shoot an item to a specific location. Use a GPS Tool with the coordinates selected to lock the cannon on target (the GPS Tool can then be removed). By default, a redstone signal will cause the cannon to fire. It could be useful for long range item transport or, with the right upgrade, as a weapon.
hqm.quest.under_pressure.advanced_air_co: You may have noticed some machines require more pressure than an air compressor can provide. To get around that, you'll have to upgrade.
Advanced pressure tubes have a capacity of 20 bar, up from the 5 bar capacity of normal pressure tubes. They can also be upgraded for further functionality.
The advanced air compressor can generate pressure at a faster rate and up to a larger capacity than the standard air compressor.
hqm.quest_set.salvage_operation.desc: Guide to scavenging resources from the ruins on the planet.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.exploration_: You may have noticed that you can't craft everything you need to survive. However, there seem to be some ruined cities scattered around. Maybe those contain resources you could use. One thing is certain, you'll need to prepare before venturing far from the shuttle.

A melee weapon of some sort would be a wise idea and perhaps some armour as well. Make sure to bring enough food and water and if you haven't set up sync shells yet, now is the time to do so. If you took the hard route, you can still craft them.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.structure_me: The ruins on this planet seem to contain remnants of all sorts of interesting technology. Some of this tech seems suited to converting matter into energy, and vice versa.
You can find a Matter-Energy Research Lab or meteorites by exploring the desert. A meteorite compass can help locate meteorites if you can't find the presses elsewhere.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.me_processor: Those broken parts won't be enough to start storing matter as energy. You'll need to make some more advanced processing circuits first.
To make processing chips, you'll need to inscribe silicon and some other materials. Make an inscriber, get some silicon, and break a PCB down into segments you can use to stitch it all together.
Use the inscriber to make the three main circuit types; logic, calculation, and engineering. You'll also need some printed silicon to use as the base plate.
When you have all the components, inscribe your circuits by putting the printed circuits on the top of the inscriber, the printed silicon on the bottom, and a PCB segment in the middle.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.me_system.de: A Matter/Energy storage system needs a few key components to work. Gather these components, construct your storage system, give it power, and you'll be able to store massive amounts of items in a tiny space.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.me_system.ta: A ME Controller is the core of a ME network. Each face of the block can accept power and provide channels to the network. There can only be one controller per network, but two controller blocks placed next to one another count as a single controller and can provide more channels than you would get from a single block. Read more in the Applied Energistics Guide.
A ME Drive houses storage cells. It can store up to 10 storage cells per drive. Colour indicators on the block indicate the status of each drive. Read more in the Applied Energistics Guide.

ME Terminals are how you access your network. The basic terminal lets you view your network's storage and add/remove items. You will likely want to upgrade to a crafting terminal very soon, and eventually a wireless terminal to access your network from anywhere. Read more in the Applied Energistics Guide.

ME Storage Cells are where items (or fluids) are stored in your network. Each item storage cell can store up to 63 types of items, with the total number of items determined by the cell's size. Generally, you should make some large storage cells to contain the items you have large amounts of, and then small storage cells to contain items you only have small amounts of. Read more in the Applied Energistics Guide.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.structure_ti: The ruins on this planet seem to contain remnants of all sorts of interesting technology. Some of these ruins have bricks that seem strong enough to withstand the searing heat of a smeltery.
You can find smeltery buildings in cities. Break the crumbling seared bricks with a hammer or put them in some kind of crushing machine to get bricks.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.smeltery.des: You are going to need lots of metal to thrive on this planet. A smeltery will help you get a good start by almost doubling how much metal you get out of each piece of ore. You can also make more advanced equipment with cast metal and alloying,
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.smeltery.tas: To construct the smeltery, make a floor out of seared bricks (3x3 is the standard), and fill every face with smeltery blocks, typically a mix of seared stone, seared drains, seared glass, and a seared tank. Place the smeltery controller in the front, and you should be able to interact with the structure. Consult the "Mighty Smelting" guide for more information.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.tinkers_anvi: The tinker's anvil is an upgrade to the tinker station that can be used to make more advanced tools, including tools that mine in an area of effect and the cleaver, great for beheading mobs.
The tinker's anvil is made from seared stone and alloyed metal blocks around a tinker station.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.cast_chest.d: When you set up a smeltery, you'll need a good place to store all your casts.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.cast_chest.t: A Cast Chest can be made from seared stone, a chest, and a cast. It stores up to 4 of each cast type, so you can usually fit all the casts you will ever need inside.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.foundry.name: Turning Up The Heat
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.foundry.desc: The foundry is an alternate version of the smeltery, it will roughly triple the number of ingots you get from ores. Ores melted in the foundry will produce an additional byproduct, providing even more resources per ore. You can even use it to get more seared stone as a byproduct of melting cobblestone. It also allows more much more liquid to be stored per block, but it can't make alloys, so you'll have to use an alloyer or the smeltery for that.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.foundry.task:
You can find foundry components in the foundry city structure.
The foundry multiblock is built in a similar way to the smeltery, but made out of foundry blocks. Unlike the smeltery, you must fill the edges of a foundry with acceptable blocks, not just the inner faces. Consult the "Fantastical Foundry" guide for more information.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.bronze_const: With a smeltery set up, you can start making tools out of alloys instead of just basic metals or other materials.

Bronze and Constantan are the two best tier III materials for weapons and tools, respectively. They have a balanced, but strong array of stats, and aren't too difficult to make with resources you likely have an abundance of. Until you find a way to make and sift nether blocks, these will generally be the best tool heads available.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.blazing_bloo: The toughest of metals require the hottest of fuels. Blazing blood is among the hottest, and is an essential ingredient for making advanced alloys.
You can make blazing blood by melting blazes in a smeltery. Blazes can be found in the Foundry structure. Small amounts of blazing blood can also be gained by melting blaze rods or blaze powder.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.manyullyn_he: Once you have found cobalt and ancient debris in a Foundry city, you can start creating advanced Tinkers' Materials. These are the two main ingredients behind the best tool materials in the game.

Manyullyn and Hepatizon are the two best tier IV materials for weapons and tools, respectively. They have a very strong array of stats, and are made from rarer nether-based materials. You will need to use blazing blood as your smeltery's fuel to create these alloys, but the investment will pay off.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.structure_nu: The ruins on this planet seem to contain remnants of all sorts of interesting technology. Some of this tech seems suitable for nuclear power generation.
You can find the nuclear plant building by exploring the desert.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.nuclear_reac: As you build your technological infrastructure you will probably find that you need more power than you can easily generate. However, now that you've gotten ahold of some nuclear reactor parts, you can get to fixing that.
You can craft the reactor terminal by repairing the parts you find in the ruins.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.turbine.name: Running on Fumes
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.turbine.desc: Need even more power? There is a solution to that. If you pipe water into a reactor it will output steam. That steam then can be used to turn a turbine, generating massive amounts of power. Of course, this isn't easy to set up. Even after you've hunted down all the components, you will need a staggering amount of water to keep things running smoothly. Generating that water will take a significant amount of time and effort to set up, but it just might be worth it if you need power in vast amounts.
hqm.quest.salvage_operation.turbine.task: Much like the reactor terminal, the turbine terminal must be made by repairing parts found in the ruins.
hqm.quest_set.technological_revolution.d: Guide to technological advancement, energy production, and machine-based automation.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.pitif: You'll need more power eventually, but making any kind of advanced machinery is difficult and often requires circuit boards. However, you can set up a basic source of power with the same fuel as a furnace.
A pitiful generator can be powered with furnace fuel, charcoal or coal blocks are especially effective. However, the power generation is slow and generally inefficient.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.condu: For further industrialisation, you'll need to move items, fluids, and energy around. Time to set up the plumbing.

Conduits are made from conduit binder and their respective materials. You can change conduit settings by right-clicking their I/O interface or right-clicking with a wrench to make quick adjustments.
Warning: Due to a bug with EnderIO and Thirst, most sources of water are unable to be transferred by fluid conduits. Other liquids will work, but we recommend using other modded transfer methods for moving water.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.manua: Alloying is an essential part of the technological revolution. The standard method of alloying is by melting the metals into a liquid and mixing the liquids together. However, you need extreme heat for that. If you can crush metals into dust, you don't need to melt them all the way to a liquid. Instead, you can just mix the metals together by hand and smelt the resulting dust back into ingots.
A mill can crush metal into dust, which can then be crafted together by hand.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.machi: The machine frame is the key to all advanced machinery. You will need an invar frame for its construction and a PCB to act as a central control circuit.
The machine frame acts as a unified base material for multiple mods.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.compr: The Compression Dynamo is the next advancement in energy generation. It generates energy in large amounts from various types of refined oils.
Diesel, Kerosene, Gasoline, LPG are some of the most practical fuels to use in the Compression Dynamo, perfect for using the oil you have refined.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.multi: The Multiservo Press can press ingots into plates, gears, and coins, as well as pack or unpack bulk items and their compressed versions.

The Multiservo Press performs different functions depending on the die used. With a packing die, it will pack items into compressed forms, equivalent to crafting recipes that fill all slots of a 2x2 or 3x3 grid. With an unpacking die, it does the reverse. Using a gearworking or nuismatic die, metals can be pressed into gears and coins. Using it without a die inserted will press ingots into plates.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.induc: The Induction Smelter can be used to process ores, produce hardened glass, and make alloys. It is an especially efficient and compact way of producing large amounts of alloys compared to alternative methods.
The induction smelter smelts up to three items together with an optional catalyst.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.pulve: The Pulverizer crushes items into dusts. It can be used to efficiently process and double ores, producing ore dust as well as a byproduct. A catalyst can be used to modify outputs, with flint being the most basic catalyst.
A Pulverizer crushes an item into dust.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.blast: The Blast Chiller cools liquids into their solid forms. It is the opposite of a Magma Crucible. It can be used to cast liquid metal into ingots, freeze water into ice or snow, and liquid redstone, glowstone, and ender pearls into their solid forms.
The Blast Chiller converts liquids into items. Some recipes require a cast, which can be made from bronze plates.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.magma: The Magma Crucible melts items into their liquid forms. It is the opposite of a Blast Chiller. It can be used to make large amounts of lava, melt plastic, and turn redstone, glowstone, and ender pearls into their liquid forms.
The magma crucible consumes items and converts them into liquids.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.phyto: The Phytogenic Insolator can grow crops without requiring them to be planted separately. It consumes a large amount of water per operation, as well as an optional catalyst. The most basic catalyst is bone meal, but with some effort, phyto-gro, an advanced fertiliser, can be crafted.

The Phytogenic Insolator takes a seed or sapling, some water, power, and an optional catalyst, and produces crops and another seed. This can be used for farming in a small space or for small-scale operations that won't need an entire farm.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.augme: Augments are upgrades that can be installed in machines to improve their speed or efficiency, add abilities, or change the way the device functions.

Augments can be installed in a machine or dynamo's augment slots. The most useful ones typically increase a machine's speed or efficiency. These usually come with drawbacks, however, and reduce their inverse property.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.inter: Internal Component upgrades modify the statistics of a machine, scaling up its base attributes. Hardened Internal Components are the first tier of Component upgrades, doubling the base stats of the machine.
Component upgrades can be installed in a machine's augment slots.

Internal Component upgrades modify the statistics of a machine, scaling up its base attributes. Reinforced Internal Components are the second tier of Component upgrades, tripling the base stats of the machine.
Component upgrades can be installed in a machine's augment slots.

Internal Component upgrades modify the statistics of a machine, scaling up its base attributes. Resonant Internal Components are the third and final tier of Component upgrades, quadrupling the base stats of the machine.
Component upgrades can be installed in a machine's augment slots.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.therm: Master thermal technology and you can move to the next stages of escaping the planet.
Use an induction smelter to make the required alloys, and submit them below.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.spawn:
If you have the means, you may want to keep animals for resources.
Chickens produce eggs, 
cows produce milk, and sheep produce wool.
The Animal Feeder provides the animals with enough food to reproduce, and the Animal Rancher automates the collection of milk and wool from cows and sheep.
You can find chicken eggs naturally, and you can craft other animal eggs in a dissolution chamber when you have a stable supply of essence.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.disso: The Dissolution Chamber allows for advanced crafting that can infuse crafted objects with liquid, sometimes producing a fluid as a byproduct.
Dissolution Chamber recipes are used to craft some advanced items with liquid meat, molten plastic, and liquid pink slime.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.mob_s: The monsters on this planet seem to emerge from the ground whenever and wherever it is dark. It may be possible to use that to your advantage. If you can funnel them towards a Mob Slaughter Factory, it will automatically grind them up into usable liquids.
A Mob Slaughter Factory can grind mobs into liquid meat and pink slime.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.plant: Planting and harvesting crops by hand is time-consuming and labour-intensive. Now that you have industrialised somewhat, it should be possible to move beyond that and automate the process.

A Plant Sower can plant crops or saplings in a small area (the range can be expanded with range upgrades). A Plant Gatherer will collect those crops and saplings.
Automating crops should provide plenty of food to eat and composting food or saplings can generate large amounts of water.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.sewag: Animals are messy, and will produce waste if left to their own devices. However, this waste can be recycled into usable materials with the right equipment. The Sewer will collect sewage and essence from animals, and the Sewage Composter will produce fertiliser from sewage.
Fertiliser can be used to grow crops just like bone meal, or be used in a Plant Fertiliser to automatically apply to plants.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.addon: Speed, Efficiency, Processing, and Range Addons are useful upgrades to many of your machines.
Most Addons come in two tiers, made with either gold or diamond gears. Range upgrades have twelve types and are not included below, but are very useful for certain machines.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.mob_c: Monsters killed with the Slaughter Factory will produce meat and slime, but that's all. Sometimes it's better to collect the materials they typically drop. A Mob Crusher can kill mobs, collecting their loot as well as their distilled essence.

The Mob Crusher will produce mob drops and essence, a type of liquid experience. Essence has a number of uses in enchantment and mob spawning. Large amounts of essence can be used to craft specific mob spawn eggs in the Dissolution Chamber.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.mecha: The monsters on this planet seem to gather wherever it is dark and prey on the living. It may be possible to lure more of them some liquid meat on energized ground.
Mechanical dirt will spawn mobs when provided with liquid meat, energy, and placed in natural spawn conditions. Fluids and energy will be carried between adjacent blocks.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.sludg: Gathering plants automatically produces a large amount of sludge as a byproduct. This sludge can be processed into some siftable blocks using a Sludge Refiner.
Provide the Sludge Refiner with sludge and energy and it will slowly process it into dirt, clay, gravel, sand, red sand, and soul sand.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.mob_d: A Mob Crusher will produce large amounts of essence. If you can capture some rarer monsters inside a Mob Imprisonment Tool, you can use that essence to duplicate that mob for future farming.

Capture a mob in the Mob Imprisonment Tool by right-clicking it. Then, place the captured mob in the Mob Duplicator to spawn copies of it. This is especially useful when farming rare mobs like Wither Skeletons.
hqm.quest.technological_revolution.indus: With many farms running, you will start collecting a lot of industrial byproducts.
Use a sewer, mob slaughter factory, and mob crusher to produce industrial byproducts. Then, convert them into useful forms using a sewage composter and dissolution chamber, and submit them below.

Until full integration and quests are built out, you're on your own. You're welcome to explore space now in its temporary state, or return to this modpack once the endgame is fully implemented. hqm.quest.to_infinity_and_beyond.metallu: Alloying typically requires mixing melted metals, but some metals can be infused together to make certain types of alloys. With a metallurgic infuser, you can make some more advanced alloys like steel. It can also make advanced control circuits, useful for all kinds of interesting mechanisms.
You can eventually upgrade the basic Metallurgic infuser to be faster, more energy efficient, and have more processing slots.

One of the most useful advanced alloys is steel. You can make steel with 2 coal and 1 iron ingot. Put the coal into the Metallurgic Infuser's infusion slot to liquefy it, then put an iron ingot into the main processing slot. This will create enriched iron, which can then be put back into the main processing slot to make steel blend. Finally, the steel blend can be smelted into a steel ingot. An enrichment chamber can be used to enrich the coal to get 8 times the resources for each piece of coal.
hqm.quest.to_infinity_and_beyond.wip_dis: Disclaimer: This modpack is still under development and the endgame has not yet been developed. Space exploration is possible with Ad Astra, but only with the default planets and very limited progression/integration.
This quest line only has placeholder quests for now. The remaining placeholders will unlock when all other quests are complete.
